{d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d) :
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let a : ℝ :=
    (∫ x : E, Set.indicator {y : E | ‖y‖ ^ 2 ≤ L} (fun y : E => ‖y‖ ^ 2) x
      ∂stdGaussian E) / r
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  Integrable (fun ω => ∑ i : Fin d, Y i ω) μ ∧
    Integrable (fun ω => ∑ i : Fin d,
      Real.cos (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ i) • Y i ω) μ ∧
    (∫ ω, ∑ i : Fin d, Y i ω ∂μ) =
      a • (1 : Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) ∧
    (∫ ω, ∑ i : Fin d, Real.cos (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ i) • Y i ω ∂μ) = 0

namespace OuterMeasure

/-- `OuterMeasure.pi m` is the finite product of the outer measures `{m i | i : ι}`.
  It is defined to be the maximal outer measure `n` with the property that
  `n (pi univ s) ≤ ∏ i, m i (s i)`, where `pi univ s` is the product of the sets
  `{s i | i : ι}`. -/
protected def pi (m : ∀ i, OuterMeasure (α i)) : OuterMeasure (∀ i, α i) :=
  boundedBy (piPremeasure m)

/-- `Measure.pi μ` is the finite product of the measures `{μ i | i : ι}`.
  It is defined to be measure corresponding to `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.pi`. -/
protected irreducible_def pi : Measure (∀ i, α i) :=
  toMeasure (OuterMeasure.pi fun i => (μ i).toOuterMeasure) (pi_caratheodory μ)

/-- The Bochner integral -/
irreducible_def integral {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : α → G) : G :=
  if _ : CompleteSpace G then
    if hf : Integrable f μ then L1.integral (hf.toL1 f) else 0
  else 0

/-- An auxiliary definition used only to construct the true `NormedAddCommGroup` (and `Metric`)
structure provided by `Matrix.instMetricSpaceL2Op` and `Matrix.instNormedAddCommGroupL2Op`. -/
@[instance_reducible]
def l2OpNormedAddCommGroupAux : NormedAddCommGroup (Matrix m n 𝕜) :=
  @NormedAddCommGroup.induced ((Matrix m n 𝕜) ≃ₗ[𝕜] (EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n →L[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 m)) _
    _ _ _ ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedAddCommGroup.toNormedAddGroup _ _ <|
    (toEuclideanLin.trans toContinuousLinearMap).injective

/-- The norm structure on `Matrix m n 𝕜` arising from the operator norm given by the identification
with (continuous) linear maps of `EuclideanSpace`. -/
@[instance_reducible]
def instL2OpNormedAddCommGroup : NormedAddCommGroup (Matrix m n 𝕜) where
  norm := l2OpNormedAddCommGroupAux.norm

definition_kinds.meaning: The original product experiment of q+1 standard d-dimensional Gaussian columns; row i collects their physical coordinate i in Euclidean(q+1)-space, under the same literal product measure.

r=q+1; L=2r+3log(1000d); a is the retained canonical row radial second moment divided by r. This scalar is a definition under stdGaussian E, not a supplied actual-row moment certificate. Its equality to every actual-row retained moment must follow internally from the canonical row law.

Source index i.val+1, midpoint angle (i.val+1-1/2)pi/d, feature0=1 and featurek=sqrt2cos(k theta). Yi is inverse-d times actual-row outer product Kronecker feature outer product when the actual row norm squared<=L; outside this closed cutoff it is zero.

definition_kinds.meaning: Paired indices are Gaussian-first in both positions. Matrix is a finite two-entry function. Integrability and Bochner integrals use the actual Matrix.Norms.L2Operator instance, identified with operators on finite Euclidean space; completeness is internally synthesized, not an extra input.

AEStronglyMeasurable and finite integral of the extended norm; the former is existence of an almost-everywhere equal strongly measurable representative. These are output obligations, never assumed. Integral notation is the Bochner integral, whose definition defaults to zero outside complete/integrable cases. The literal integrable outputs prevent using that default as a fake mean identity.

Every actual Yi is integrable and its exact matrix expectation is a/d times I tensor ti ti-transpose. This gives no scalar bias/range estimate for a, no iid claim, and no new public row-law or radial-moment theorem.

Both actual finite sums on the same outcome space are integrable; their Bochner expectations are a times identity and zero. The weighted sum uses precisely cos((2q+1)theta_i). These are actual integrals of sums, requiring internal integral exchange, and not caller-supplied formal mean matrices.
